[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Mapletree Investments was established on December 18, 2000 as a wholly owned subsidiary of Temasek Holdings, the Singapore state investment company, originating from PSA Corporations transfer of non-port properties. Per Wikipedia, Mapletree is a global real estate firm managing three Singapore-listed REITs and nine private equity funds, overseeing roughly 77.4 billion Singapore dollars in assets across logistics, office, retail, mixed-use, industrial, data centre, student housing, and residential properties in 13 markets including the United States, though the Wikipedia summary consulted this session did not specifically describe Georgia operations.

The registrys own sourced page for this facility, a Mapletree Industrial Trust property listing, directly identifies the Alpharetta, Georgia address at 1001 Windward Concourse as a Mapletree Industrial Trust property; Mapletree Industrial Trust is one of the Singapore-listed REITs managed by parent Mapletree Investments. This specific facility, recorded in this registry as Mapletree Industrial in Alpharetta, Georgia, was not individually named in any prior operator-level research; its operator field was blank in the source data and is set here to Mapletree Industrial Trust, directly corroborated by the trusts own property listing for this exact address.

reading.body:
Mapletree Industrial in Alpharetta, Georgia, is operated by , but no IT capacity in megawatts has been published for this facility.

Without a published capacity figure, the facility cannot be sized against other data centers in this collection, or judged for whether it could plausibly host AI training infrastructure, which typically requires tens of megawatts and up. What is on record is the facility's location and operator, not its scale.

No compliance certifications are published for Mapletree Industrial. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

Georgia has 7 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 4 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 66.3 MW.
